about.title: About Annuity Calculator - Retirement Income Planning Tool
about.description: The Annuity Calculator is a financial planning tool designed to help you estimate annuity payments, future values, and retirement income streams. Whether you're planning for retirement, evaluating annuity products, or calculating periodic payments, this calculator provides formula-based projections for both immediate and deferred annuities. Understanding annuity calculations can support retirement planning, as some annuities provide contract-based income streams and may be one part of a broader retirement portfolio.

howTo.title: How to Use the Annuity Calculator

steps.title: Choose Annuity Type
steps.description: Select between immediate annuity (starts paying immediately) or deferred annuity (starts paying at a future date).

steps.title: Enter Principal Amount
steps.description: Input the initial investment amount or lump sum you plan to invest in the annuity.

steps.title: Set Interest Rate
steps.description: Enter the annual interest rate or quoted contract rate offered by the annuity provider.

steps.title: Payment Period
steps.description: Specify the payment frequency (monthly, quarterly, annually) and total payment period.

steps.title: Payment Options
steps.description: Choose between fixed payments for a set period or lifetime payments with survivor benefits.

steps.title: Review Results
steps.description: Analyze the payment amounts, total returns, and income projections for your retirement planning.

faq.q: What's the difference between immediate and deferred annuities?
faq.a: Immediate annuities start paying income within one year of purchase, while deferred annuities accumulate value for a period before payments begin. Immediate annuities are commonly used for current income needs, while deferred annuities are more often used for future retirement planning.

Annuity payments are calculated based on the principal amount, interest rate, payment period, and your life expectancy (for lifetime annuities). The calculator uses actuarial tables and compound interest formulas to determine payment amounts.

faq.q: Are annuities a good investment for retirement?
faq.a: Some annuities offer contract-based income features and tax-deferred growth, which may make them useful in retirement planning. However, they often have higher fees than other investments. Review your risk tolerance, income needs, contract terms, and other retirement assets when evaluating annuities.

faq.q: What happens to my annuity when I die?
faq.a: This depends on the annuity type and options you choose. Some annuities end at death, while others provide survivor benefits to beneficiaries. Joint and survivor annuities continue payments to a surviving spouse, though typically at a reduced amount.
